extractions.description: Introduces and executes PoisonBench, a benchmark for evaluating language-model vulnerability to poisoned preference data through content-injection and alignment-deterioration attacks across multiple LLM backbones, datasets, preference-learning procedures, triggers, poison ratios, and defenses.

type.quote: Using P OISON B ENCH, we evaluate several widely used LLMs of various sizes and architectures.
type.justification: The paper runs poisoning, fine-tuning, inference, evaluation, ablation, and defense experiments.

name.quote: These results expose weaknesses in current preference learning techniques, highlighting the urgent need for more robust defenses against malicious models and data manipulation.
name.justification: The work studies the security and robustness of learned systems against poisoning.
